entities.name: PMID:27499954
observations: Retrospective open Ivor-Lewis cohort of 208 patients: 121 received mediastinal omental transposition and 87 did not.
Transposition was associated with lower intrathoracic infection (30.6% vs 48.3%, P=0.009), lower infection severity (P=0.005), and independent protection against infection (OR 0.415, P=0.007).
Pharmacy cost was lower with transposition (¥21,668 vs ¥27,012, P=0.010), while total in-hospital cost was not significantly different.

entities.name: PMID:25273661
observations: Retrospective cohort of 148 patients: 84 received mediastinal omental transposition and 64 did not.
Intrathoracic infection was lower with transposition (39.3% vs 56.2%); among infected patients, combined sepsis was lower (57.6% vs 86.1%).
The abstract did not report pharmacy or total cost outcomes.

entities.name: Omental transposition outcomes
observations: Two retrospective single-center comparative cohorts consistently associated mediastinal omental transposition with fewer or less severe intrathoracic infections after Ivor-Lewis esophagectomy.
Lower pharmacy cost was reported in one cohort, but overall hospital cost was not significantly reduced and cost evidence was not replicated in the second cohort.
Observational evidence supports an association but does not establish causality.
